title: Java
subtitle: Modern Java on JDK 25, from a first program to records, pattern matching, virtual threads and the tools professionals use every day.
description: Java is a statically typed, object-oriented language that compiles to bytecode for the Java Virtual Machine, so one program runs on any operating system and processor. Since 1995 it has become one of the most widely used languages in the world: it runs the back ends of banks, airlines and online shops, much of the big-data ecosystem, and countless enterprise and Android applications. Modern Java (records, sealed types, pattern matching, streams and virtual threads) is far more concise than its old reputation suggests.

This course is for anyone who can already write a small program with variables, decisions and loops, at the level of the [Start level of Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience. It takes you from installing the JDK and running a first program, through the core language and its type system, to collections and streams, data-oriented programming, exceptions, concurrency, the JVM's garbage collectors and JIT compiler, and the build and test tools of professional teams, ending with a complete small project.

To run the code, install a JDK, version 25 or newer: free builds are available from [jdk.java.net](https://jdk.java.net/) and [Eclipse Temurin](https://adoptium.net/). For short snippets with nothing installed, use the official [Java Playground](https://dev.java/playground/). Every complete program in these lessons was compiled and run on JDK 25 with `java Main.java`.
